\[ \text{Time} = \frac{\text{Distance}}{\text{Speed}} \]

\[ \text{Time}_{\text{fast lane}} = \frac{480 \text{ miles}}{60 \text{ miles/hour}} = 8 \text{ hours} \]

Step 3: Time taken by the car in the slow lane
Since both cars are covering the same distance (480 miles), the time taken by the car in the slow lane can be calculated using the same formula as above:
\[ \text{Time}_{\text{slow lane}} = \frac{480 \text{ miles}}{30 \text{ miles/hour}} = 16 \text{ hours} \]

Therefore, the time taken by the car in the slow lane to cover the same distance is **16 hours**.

3B = 24 \\
B = \frac{24}{3} \\
B = 8
\]

\[
S = 2B \\
S = 2 \times 8 \\
S = 16
\]
